question: A summarizer loops 6 times on a 3-page doc. On a 400-page doc it runs 190 turns and times out. The team sets max_turns: 200. What is wrong with that number?
ideal: 200 is the number that just failed, so it licenses 199 turns of the same runaway
the cap should come from the p99 of HEALTHY runs, which excludes this incident by definition
turns are a proxy for the resource actually paid (tokens / dollars / wall clock) and the proxy drifts when the model changes
name an owner: a cap nobody is paged for is a config value, not a control

question: Your agent has a 90-second timeout and no turn cap. It never times out and the monthly bill triples. In one sentence, why did the timeout not help?
ideal: a timeout ends a run that is STUCK; this run is working
a cap ends a run that is working and will not stop
healthy and unbounded are compatible states

question: A PR swaps LangGraph for CrewAI. Tests pass. Name the class of thing that can disappear without a single test failing, and why no test catches it.
ideal: controls implemented as framework callbacks: identity/principal, spend quota, trace fields, eval gate
the run still SUCCEEDS after the swap, it is simply no longer governed, so a pass/fail test has nothing to assert on
the rule: anything that must survive the swap is harness, not framework

question: Give the one-line difference between orchestration and governance, then say which one a framework owns.
ideal: orchestration decides what runs NEXT; governance decides what is allowed to run AT ALL and what is recorded
the framework owns orchestration
governance must survive a framework swap

question: Your provider silently updates gpt-4o to a new snapshot. No fallback fired, no release shipped, quality drops 8%. Which layer should have made this visible, and what field on the trace?
ideal: observability / governance (L3) is the layer
the field is the RESOLVED model id on the response span (gpt-4o-2024-11-20), not the requested alias (gpt-4o)
record the alias only and the swap is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION, because the field never changes
alert on a change in the distribution of that id, not on its value
scored_on: the chain from alias to invisible

question: A fallback and a silent provider swap both change which model answered. What does one leave behind that the other does not?
ideal: a fallback is declared, so a fired-fallback event exists on the trace
a silent swap has no event at all
both changed the model; only one is observable

question: 03:00. Agent spend is 40x baseline. Latency normal. No deploy in 6 days. Success rate flat. Give cues, expectancies, plausible goal, ONE action, and the observation that would prove you wrong.
ideal: cues: spend moved and latency did not; no deploy; success rate flat
expectancies: turns-per-run up, tokens-per-turn flat
goal: stop the bleed without killing a working feature
action: check whether the cap is denominated in turns while the model got chattier
killer simulation: a retry storm would move latency too; latency is flat, so not retries

question: Nightly rubric falls 84% to 76% over nine days. No release, no prompt change, one model family only. Fill the five slots.
ideal: cues: gradual not stepwise; scoped to one family; no change on your side
expectancies: resolved model ids in the window are not all identical
goal: name the day it changed before arguing about the rubric
action: diff the resolved-model-id distribution for the window against the prior month
killer simulation: if the id distribution is flat, this is input drift and the model is innocent

question: A 4,000-line PR swaps the agent framework. Tests pass, two approvals. Fill the five slots.
ideal: cues: tests pass on a governance-adjacent swap; diff mentions no identity or trace code
expectancies: if governance is outside the framework, no control lives under the framework directory
goal: keep every control that exists today and know which were on loan
action: list controls (principal, spend cap, trace fields, eval gate) and name the file each lives in
killer simulation: if every control is already outside the framework directory, the swap is cheap and the objection is theatre
